issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as an int (problem_statement.md lines 26-28), but the solution's RollerCoaster class provides a getter getNumberOfLoopings() that returns double (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java lines 5-14). This is a return-type mismatch: the attribute is int but the public getter returns double. Students following the specification will implement a getter returning int, causing signature/test mismatches and confusion about the correct type.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the getter's return type consistent with the attribute's declared type in the UML. Change the solution's getter to return int (e.g. public int getNumberOfLoopings() { return numberOfLoopings; }) so it matches the attribute type in the problem statement. Alternatively, if double was intended, update the UML/problem statement to declare numberOfLoopings as double — but keeping it as int and changing the getter to int is the recommended fix.
